In the Shiur of last week we were discussing the principles of Dibur in the sense of Halachos in the Torah, which Halachos in the Torah can be affected through a Dibur, which don't even require Dibur.

But there is a Gemara that appears in the second Perek of Masechet Kiddushin, Daf Mem-Tes, which is a critical Gemara in terms of our whole understanding of the relationship of Dibur and Machshava as relates to many many Halachos in the Torah.
That's a Sugya, the famous Sugya, the Gemara tells the following story.
There was an individual who was planning on going to Eretz Yisrael and he was planning on selling all his property, he lived in Bavel, he wanted to sell his house.
So he went out and he sold his house to somebody but he didn't bother telling the person that the reason why he sold the house is because he's planning on going on Aliyah.
And then his plans fell through, so what happens, Epes ba-Nefesh, he had to put things on hold and he ended up not going to Eretz Yisrael.
So now he's out of a house.
So he comes to the Koneh, he comes to the person who he bought the house from and he says, 'Listen, I only sold you the house because I thought I was moving to Eretz Yisrael.
Whatever Nitgal ha-Davar, I never ended up going, it turns out that the house was all a Mekach Ta'ut, it's all on the understanding that I was going to Eretz Yisrael.
I'm not going so I want the house back.
So I want to cancel the sale.' So this entire case came to Rava.
So the Shailoh was how do you Pasken such a case?
On the one hand the guy is telling us the truth that he was only planning on selling the house על מנת לעלות לארץ ישראל.
On the other hand he didn't tell us at the time.
So the Gemara says the conclusion of the Sugya was that דברים שבלב אינם דברים.
That if he would have actually stipulated, he would have actually said and made a conditional sale, so we know that there is a Parsha in the Torah of making sales al tnai.

The Gemara tells us in Masechet Kiddushin a little bit later on in the third Perek that if a guy Me-Kadesh a woman on the condition that it rains today or Me-Garesh a woman on the condition XYZ, I sell you a field on the condition XYZ, so we learn out from Parshat Matot that what's called the תנאי בני גד ובני ראובן that Moshe Rabbeinu gave the whole Ever ha-Yarden, east side of the Yarden to בני גד ובני ראובן al tnai on the condition that they're going to come and fight on the west side of the Yarden.
So it was a matana al tnai and it says B'Feirush in the Torah that if you do the Tnai you get the Kinyan, if you don't get the Tnai then you don't get the Kinyan.

So the Gemara says we derive from here a Din in Choshen Mishpat and in Even ha-Ezer that you can make a Mechir al tnai, Matana al tnai, Kiddushin al tnai, Gittin al tnai, it's a whole Parsha of Tnaim in the Torah.
So comes the Gemara and says should we view this as a Mechir al tnai?
The Gemara says no you can't, you know why?
Because he didn't say it.
Because he may have thought that he was selling it al tnai but he didn't stipulate, he didn't say it explicitly, not in writing, not in a verbal, not in nothing.
He had in his mind that he's selling it al tnai.
So the Gemara says that's what constitutes a Dvarim sheb'lev.
So דברים שבלב אינם דברים.
The Torah is not Misyaches to what a person has in his mind.
We only take into consideration what a person actually said.
So on that Sugya the Rashba is Ba'al Kushya.
How can we say there is a Din of דברים שבלב אינם דברים?
דברים שבלב אינם דברים is not true.
It's contradicted by last week's Sugya.
We spoke about that the Torah does give certain credibility to what a person thinks.
The Torah says you can be Mafrish Trumah by Machshava.
The Torah says you can be Makdish things by Machshava.
We said last week maybe you can take on yourself Mitzvos by Machshava, maybe you can Hitchayiv yourself Tzedakah by Machshava.
There is a Parsha in the Torah of Dvarim sheb'lev.
There are Dinim in the Torah that do, the Torah does recognize what a person has in his heart.
So how do you resolve that contradiction?
On the one hand we just Machak away, we just negate דברים שבלב אינם דברים.
On the other hand אף על פי כן sometimes the Torah does take Dvarim sheb'lev.
So if you would have asked me I would have said it's not a Kushya in the first place, I'd say that's a Gzeirat ha-Katuv.
V'nechshav lachem trumaschem.
Every case that we spoke about last week where Dvarim sheb'lev kicks in, that's because there's a special Pasuk to that effect.
Otherwise under normal circumstances the starting point is everything has to be verbalized.
The Torah is not speaking to people's hearts and innermost feelings.
In terms of Dinei Mamonos, in terms of Halachos, in terms of Issur v'Hetter, we care what you're saying, not what you're thinking.
So that's what I would have said.
But the Rashba doesn't say that.
The Rashba says a different Vort.
The Rashba explains that in Lomdus Dvarim sheb'lev doesn't apply here.
Dvarim sheb'lev means when I do a Ma'aseh or I do a Dibur and now we want to go into the deep recesses of your mind and be Mevatel what you said.
So now we have a contradiction.

On the one hand you said I'm selling you the field, you went through the motions of selling the field and now you're telling a story that oh yeah by the way you didn't really mean to sell the field except for XYZ takes place.
You didn't say that.
You didn't do that.
So everything that you did and said is pointing in one direction and now you're telling your Machshava and Ipcha in the other direction.
So that's what the Gemara means that דברים שבלב אינם דברים.
דברים שבלב אינם דברים לבטל דברים שבפה.
But Dvarim sheb'lev in and of themselves, can you have, can the Torah grant...
This principle דברים שבלב אינם דברים, are there any limitations to this principle?
So the Gemara has in Masechet Bava Batra an important limitation.
We spoke about this in other contexts before.
The Gemara says that bameh devarim amurim that devarim shebalev can't cancel a devarim shebepeh, that's only when it's not so clear what the person's machshavah was.
You see a guy sells land, you take a survey, how many people sell land because they're going to Eretz Yisrael?
Sometimes, buy a lot of houses here are sold, guys moving to Eretz Yisrael.
Not always.
A guy puts up a for sale sign, maybe he's planning on moving around the corner.
So how do you know why a person is selling his land?
Eich tesei?
So comes the, comes the Gemara and says when you have a devarim shebalev that wasn't easily guessed at by everybody, I know why he's selling a land?
If you wanted to tell me why you're selling your land, tell me why you're selling your land.
You didn't tell me, I can assume that you're selling it for not limited to any particular reason.
But what if you have a situation where it's so obvious from context what we call דברים שבלבו ובלב כל אדם?
The Gemara doesn't use that phrase, the Rishonim use that phrase.
The Gemara uses the phrase umdena.
Umdena means that it's so obvious to us, we look at it, we see an umdena de'muchach.
It's so clear as day that you're trying to do X, Y, and Z because of reason A, B, C.
So the Gemara says that's a whole different ballgame.
So whenever you, the Gemara says מאן תנא דאזיל בתר אומדנא?

The Gemara quotes Tannaim who say that when you have an umdena, it's umdena de'muchach, it's so obvious that that's what you're doing, then we will take into consideration the quote unquote devarim shebalev.
That's no longer devarim shebalev, that's the phrase that we coined, דברים שבלבו ובלב כל אדם.
So the Gemara gives some examples of this.
The Gemara says let's say a person makes a wild statement.

Why is that?
Because he doesn't think that he has any children.
But let's say it turns out that he does have a child, he didn't even realize that he had a child.
He was married, he had a wife in medinas hayam, he didn't even realize that he has a child.
So the Gemara says a guy makes this sweeping statement, he's giving away every last penny to somebody before he dies, and then halo hadavar, he finds out that he had a, that he really has a child.

So the Gemara says it's so obvious that the person never would have given such a matanah even though he didn't say it, he didn't say, Reuven didn't say I'm giving a matanah because I don't have any children.

He said I'm giving away a matanah but everybody realizes from context what normal person does that if he has a child?
So the Gemara gives that as an example, other examples where you have this umdena de'muchach.
So umdena de'muchach trumps the principle of דברים שבלב אינם דברים.
Then and only then we would take into consideration devarim shebalev.
You could say that that's called דברים שבלבו ובלב כל אדם.
